newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends up on commercials, spreads, CBOT.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends up on commercials, spreads, CBOT.

text.p: WCE canola futures ended up on commercial demand, spreads and CBOT soybeans, traders said.

"We had commercial buying and local spreading," a trader said. Mar-July spread at $1, Nov-Jan $4.20, May-July $1.20. November crush margin ended down at -25.08 from Wednesday's close at -24.04. Volume was 4,300 lots with 200 hedges.
Japan bought 2,000 to 3,000 tonnes, sources said.

January canola was up $1.90 at $393.50, above technical resistance level of $392, with other months $1.80 to $2.60 higher. Flaxseed ended mostly up on commercial buying with spreading the feature. January flax was up $1 at $360.
Nov-Jan spread at $2.50, Jan-Mar $2.50. Volume was 450.
Western barley futures ended mostly up, supported by gains in CBOT corn and early short-covering ahead of next Tuesday's key USDA crop output report. The WCE is closed on Monday.

Slow farmer sales were also supportive for both barley and wheat markets. February western barley was up $1.40 at $139.30 with December wheat up $0.50 at $164.10. Barley volume was 1,310 lots and wheat volume was 1,000 lots.
UGG sold 150 December peas down US$0.50 to US$195.50 to PCTS and Louis Dreyfus, traders said.
(All values in Canadian dollars except peas, oats).
